A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain complete main texts and appendices A–G. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support matching their equations, tables, and figures despite layout shifts.

before.justification: v3 reports original NeRF classification, retrieval, captioning, and question-answering experiments in Section 4, with additional results in Appendices C, E, and F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including the main experimental tables and appendix analyses and qualitative examples.

M1.justification: The parameter-graph construction, GMN encoder, nf2vec decoder, rendering and contrastive objectives, and inference procedure remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A–B.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ShapenetRender and Objaverse NeRF datasets, ShapeNeRF–Text supervision, and 13 architectures across three families. Classification, retrieval, language tasks, and generalization scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator participation is unchanged: nf2vec and Cardace et al. in applicable classification experiments, RANDOM in retrieval, and LLaNA in single-architecture language comparisons. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix B retain the same splits, preprocessing, architecture configurations, training budgets, and evaluation metrics, including 250-epoch encoder training with batch size 8.

E4.justification: The loss-component comparisons, t-SNE analysis, unseen-architecture evaluations, Objaverse generalization tests, and retrieval failure examples are unchanged. Moving Figure 3 does not introduce a new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experimental results. Statistical reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 2–13 and 15–24 retain identical scores and result entries. For example, Table 3 reports 93.6% for the proposed rendering-loss model versus 92.1% for nf2vec on MLP in both versions. The plotted and qualitative results also match.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, mathematical definitions, and Appendix A's graph-size and memory-efficiency reasoning are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: v4 drops dataset creation and future release as a separately enumerated contribution in the introduction, while retaining the datasets and announcing availability in the abstract. The central method, generalization, novelty, and performance claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretation of rendering versus contrastive objectives, architecture-specific weaknesses, retrieval failures, and limitations concerning predominantly ShapenetRender-based evaluation.

D1.justification: v3 promises a future code and dataset release in the introduction and Appendix D. v4 replaces this with an abstract statement of availability and a concrete project hyperlink. Implementation details, hardware, and training times are unchanged; the linked resources were not inspected.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior NeRF, meta-network, and contrastive-learning research are unchanged. Added bibliography page back-references are navigation changes, not new citations.

P1.justification: v4 updates the publication header and author/affiliation presentation, shortens the contribution list, and makes a small grammatical correction in Appendix D. Section order and explanatory prose otherwise remain stable.

P2.justification: Figure 3 moves from page 7 to page 6, with associated text and table repositioning. v4 also revises the title-page layout and adds colored hyperlinks and bibliography back-references. Figure content and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 provides a concrete code/data access link where v3 only promised a future release, improving reproducibility guidance. Internal hyperlinks and bibliography back-references also improve navigation. These are limited documentation gains: the scientific evidence and limitations are unchanged, and the linked resources themselves were not assessed.
